comments.body: `_mask_hidden_input` does not skip the empty string, contrary to its own docstring. The guard is `if value is not None:`, so for `value == ""` the pattern becomes `(?<!\w)(?!\w)`, which matches at every position where neither neighbour is a word character. Any message containing punctuation or whitespace runs gets `'***'` injected into it, e.g. `"x, y"` becomes `"x'***' y"`. The empty value can reach this code via `prompt(..., default="")`. Fix: guard with `if value:` (or skip when empty) so the docstring contract holds.

The `hide_input` and non-`hide_input` error paths now share the msgid `"Error: {message}"`, which replaces the previous `"Error: {e.message}"` msgid for the non-hidden path. Existing translations keyed on `Error: {e.message}` no longer match, so all localised error prompts regress to English. This is a regression on the path most users hit, and the recent localisation commit (5b9630f) makes it a real cost. Keep the original msgid for the non-hidden branch, or migrate the catalogue, and say so in the PR.

Behavioural regression in the masking semantics: the old code fell back to a generic message whenever the raw value appeared anywhere in the error. The new word-boundary lookarounds only mask standalone occurrences. A value embedded in a larger token (e.g. password `abc` appearing in `xabcx`, or `a.b` in `a.bc`) is now shown verbatim, which is a partial leak of the secret. The PR also removes the generic fallback entirely, so the existing `partial-word-match-falls-back-to-generic` case in tests/test_termui.py likely no longer exercises what its id says.

Examples: a secret `secret` inside `secret_key` or `secret123`, and a secret ending in a non-word character such as `x+` inside `x+y`. In each case the password's bytes still appear in the error text that `hide_input=True` is meant to suppress. The old code avoided this by falling back to a generic message when the raw value was present. The new code masks only whole-token occurrences and passes the rest through, which is a leak.
